methodological_rigor.justification: This phase Ib dose-expansion cohort study of izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren, bispecific EGFR/HER3 ADC) enrolled 83 NSCLC patients across four genomic alteration cohorts at five centers in China. Primary endpoint was safety; efficacy (ORR, DCR, DOR, PFS) was secondary or exploratory. Statistical analysis is descriptive with Clopper-Pearson CIs for binary endpoints and Kaplan-Meier estimation for time-to-event outcomes. The prespecified subgroup analyses by GA cohort are appropriate. Key methodological limitations include: single-arm non-randomized design, exclusively Chinese patient population (5 centers) limiting generalizability, local investigator-assessed tumor response without central review (RECIST v1.1), short median follow-up (7.3 months) with immature OS data (14.1% events), and heterogeneous prior treatment histories across cohorts. The prespecification of the cohort analysis is a strength, as is the systematic stratification by GA type.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase Ib single-arm study (Oxford LoE 4) with high translational relevance in therapeutically challenging NSCLC subtypes. The overall ORR of 39.7-46.2% and median PFS of 7.0 months in a heterogeneous pretreated population is clinically meaningful, particularly the EGFR exon20ins/nonclassical confirmed ORR of 69.2% (mPFS 10.5 months) and HER2-mutant ORR of 52.9% (mPFS 7.5 months) in patients who had exhausted available targeted therapies. The bispecific EGFR/HER3 ADC approach offers potential utility across multiple GA subtypes that lack effective post-progression options (KRAS/BRAF/MET, ALK/ROS1/RET fusions). Clinical impact is currently limited to hypothesis generation pending randomized phase II/III validation.

reporting_quality.justification: The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05194982) and China Drug Trials (CTR20212923) with ethics approvals and GCP compliance documented. Safety reporting follows NCI CTCAE v5.0, and RECIST v1.1 tumor response criteria are applied. Patient flow diagram, baseline characteristics, and safety/efficacy tables are provided. Key limitations in reporting include: local investigator tumor assessment without central review, no independent data monitoring committee for efficacy endpoint validation, limited biomarker data for response prediction (no correlative tissue analyses reported), and absence of protocol deposition or individual patient-level data in a public repository. The Chinese-only enrollment and use of CSCO guidelines for prior treatment standards limit applicability outside China.

novelty_literature.justification: Iza-bren is the first bispecific ADC (targeting both EGFR and HER3 simultaneously) to demonstrate clinical activity across a broad range of NSCLC genomic alteration subtypes in a single prespecified multicohort trial. The concept of leveraging EGFR/HER3 co-targeting for tumors driven by non-ERBB oncogenes (KRAS, BRAF, MET) represents a novel mechanistic hypothesis with supporting activity (ORR 40%, including KRAS G12C 4/8 cPR). The 85.7% confirmed ORR in EGFR exon20ins patients with prior chemotherapy and limited prior targeted therapy exposure, and the manageable ILD rate (1.4% vs. 9.7-12.9% for T-DXd), distinguish iza-bren in the competitive ADC landscape for NSCLC.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with logical progression from study design through safety, overall efficacy, and subgroup-specific results. The GA cohort structure and inclusion criteria are clearly described. The discussion thoughtfully contextualizes results against established standards (amivantamab, sunvozertinib for EGFR exon20ins; T-DXd, zongertinib for HER2-mutant) and acknowledges limitations including the rapidly evolving treatment landscape. The limitations section is appropriately comprehensive, noting the single-arm design, Chinese-only population, short follow-up, and local assessment. The reference to the first-in-human phase Ia publication provides necessary dose rationale context.

key_strengths: First multicohort phase Ib trial of a bispecific EGFR/HER3 ADC across diverse non-classical NSCLC genomic alteration subtypes, with encouraging ORR of 69.2% in EGFR exon20ins/nonclassical and 52.9% in HER2-mutant cohorts
Novel proof-of-concept for bispecific ADC activity in KRAS/BRAF/MET-driven NSCLC (ORR 40%), supporting the hypothesis that ERBB pathway co-targeting retains activity beyond ERBB-driven tumors
Favorable ILD rate (1.4% grade 2) compared to T-DXd class precedent, suggesting a potentially differentiated safety profile for the bispecific design
Prespecified four-cohort subgroup structure and comprehensive safety monitoring with 47% dose reduction rate providing clear dose management guidance for future trials
key_concerns: Single-arm, non-randomized, China-only phase Ib trial with local investigator-assessed endpoints and heterogeneous prior treatment histories precludes definitive efficacy conclusions or cross-trial comparisons

Short median follow-up (7.3 months) with immature OS data (14.1% events) and unconfirmed partial responses in 5 patients limits durability assessment; most patients had not been exposed to current standard-of-care agents (amivantamab, sunvozertinib, T-DXd) limiting clinical context
chief_reviewer.rationale: This phase Ib study provides early-phase proof-of-concept for iza-bren across multiple NSCLC GA subtypes, with particularly encouraging activity in EGFR exon20ins and HER2-mutant cohorts. The novel bispecific ADC mechanism and broad genomic scope of activity support publication in a Tier 2 journal with minor revisions addressing the China-only generalizability concerns and the need for central response assessment in future studies.
